steps.text: Flat shapes are shapes that lie on a page. A circle, a square, a rectangle and a triangle are all flat shapes.
A clock is round like a circle. A book cover is a rectangle. A slice of pizza is like a triangle.
Look around your room. Find one thing shaped like a circle and one shaped like a square.
Solid shapes can be picked up and held. A cube, a cuboid, a sphere, a cylinder and a cone are all solid shapes.
A dice is a cube. A can of juice is a cylinder. A ball is a sphere. An ice cream cone is a cone.
Find a box at home. Is it a cube or a cuboid? Check if all its sides are the same size.
A face is a flat side of a solid shape. An edge is where two faces meet. A corner is where edges meet.
A cube has 6 flat faces, 12 edges and 8 corners. Count them on a dice.
Pick up a box. Run your finger along one edge, then touch one corner.
Skip counting means counting by jumps instead of one by one. We can skip count by 2s, 5s or 10s.
Counting by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Each jump adds 5.
Count your fingers and toes by 5s. Say the numbers out loud as you go.
A number pattern follows a rule. Once you find the rule, you can guess what comes next.
2, 4, 6, 8, __. Each number is 2 more than the last, so the next number is 10.
Write your own pattern that adds 3 each time. Start at 1.
Sometimes a number in a pattern is hidden. Look at the numbers before and after it to find the rule.
10, 20, __, 40. The rule is add 10, so the missing number is 30.
Ask a friend to hide one number in a counting pattern. Find it using the rule.
A repeating pattern uses the same group of shapes or colours again and again.
Red, blue, red, blue, red, blue is a repeating pattern with two colours.
Make a pattern with two colours of beads, blocks or drawings.
A shape has symmetry if you can fold it in half and both sides match exactly.
A circle, a square and the letter A all have a line of symmetry.
Fold a piece of paper in half. Cut a shape along the fold and open it up.
Tiling means covering a space with shapes that fit together with no gaps.
Square tiles fit together neatly on a floor with no space between them.
Look at the floor tiles at home or school. What shape are they?
In a number like 4,236, each digit has a place: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
In 4,236: 4 is thousands, 2 is hundreds, 3 is tens, 6 is ones.
Pick a 4-digit number. Say out loud what each digit's place is.
Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the value of each digit.
5,821 in expanded form is 5000 + 800 + 20 + 1.
Write your house number or a bus number in expanded form.
To add or subtract big numbers, line up the ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, then work column by column.
2,450 + 1,300 = 3,750. Add ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands.
Add the prices of two things you know, like 1,200 and 1,500.
